note: Townsfolk greet the Avatar by deed (PLAN-VIRTUES.md 5.11; game/world_stages.h). Engine-driven barks, only with Virtues on and from stage 1. Now and then (every `check` frames, chance `chance` by stage, stage 0 first) a person on a town map standing within `range` of the Avatar, not busy (no conversation, scene, fight or other bark), says one line. Each person greets at most once in `person_wait` frames, and nobody does within `wait` frames of the last greeting. Greeters are people: the named townsfolk (shapes with no row in the monster table) and people_shapes; never a monster, a child (not_shapes) or anyone in a fight. A line needs its `key` (a paid virtue key 'Virtue/key' or 'mark/<m>', as in virtues.json's epilogue) and `min_stage`; deed lines not yet heard go first. `who`: 'town' (anyone but a guard), 'guard' (shape 574) or 'any'. {you} becomes 'Avatar' once the mark known_avatar is set, else 'stranger'; {You} the same, capitalised.
not_npcs_note: Never greet: 7 Mordea (she ordered Toran's death).

lines.text: You're the one who spoke up for Toran's family.
Rhian says you gave her obsidian for the gem cutter's kin. That was kindly done.
They cleared Toran's name, and they say it was your doing. Bless you, {you}.
Toran's name is clean now. I stood guard at his beheading. I'm glad of it, {you}.
You kept your word to Devon. Folk here remember that.
The boats are out on the lake again! My cousin brought in a fine catch.
Rhian is grieving, but she says you told her true. She's glad of that.
My little one plays Heroes and Monsters all day now. You're always the hero, {you}.
Even the Necromancers speak well of you. Strange times, {you}.
They say the Cemetery has gone quiet. Was that you, {you}?
You stood in the streets with us when the dead came. Tenebrae won't forget.
You fought beside the watch that night. Any time you need a hand, {you}.
Is it true you went into Khumash-Gor's tomb and came out again?
Good day to you, {you}.
Fine weather, for once.
Good day, {you}. Keep safe out there.
Things feel lighter of late, don't they?
Pardon me, {you}. Mind the step there.
Folk are talking about you, {you}. Good talk, mostly.
There goes the one everybody speaks of! Good day, {you}!
An honour, {you}. The watch is at your service.
My mother says the sun shines brighter since you came, {you}.
